mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority or passport issuing authority in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if country is HCCH 1961 Apostille Convention signatory) or Consular Legalization (if not)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or tax assessment older than 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Municipal registry / local public utility / tax authority in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization if not an official multilingual document; otherwise Hague Apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of any corporate UBO (where applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry or competent corporate authority in the UBO's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (depending on jurisdiction)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, authorized signatories, and relevant beneficial owners against UN Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, CSSF blacklist, and Luxembourg PEP lists. Screening must be performed pre-incorporation and repeated at least every six months or upon any triggering event. Enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs, including verification of source of wealth and source of funds.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), available at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in Latin script. The legal form element 'SCSp' or 'société en commandite spéciale' must appear in full or abbreviated. The name may be in French, German, or Luxembourgish, or in another language provided it is transliterated into Latin characters and is not misleading as to the legal form or public nature of the entity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name reservation is rejected by the RCS registrar, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) within 15 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must be submitted via the LBR electronic portal, attaching a legal justification memorandum and supporting documents. If the administrative appeal is denied, a further judicial appeal may be lodged before the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg within three months of the denial. No automatic extension of the initial reservation is available; the applicant may re-apply after the rejection resolution or while the appeal is pending, subject to availability of the name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible as the statutory registered office of an SCSp, provided a registered domiciliation agent is appointed in Luxembourg. For low-risk 3PL fulfillment/kitting activities, a sheltered virtual office is accepted; however, genuine economic substance in Luxembourg is required to avoid tax residency or anti-abuse challenges. The SCSp must be able to demonstrate real direction, decision-making, and management in a Luxembourg physical or compliant outsource capacity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: estimated annual probability of unannounced physical inspection below 5% for a private SCSp not subject to financial supervision. Probability may rise to 10–15% if the entity holds a VAT number or exhibits unusual trade patterns.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation (SCSp) and drafting of partnership agreement
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: EUR 1,500–2,500 plus statutory notarial tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration in the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff: EUR 75 registration fee plus EUR 2 stamp duty

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of incorporation deed in RESA (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés)
Filing of Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) information in the RBE register
Consular legalization and/or apostille of UBO documents and sworn translation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs / consular post / sworn translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular fee schedule; translation at market rate ~USD 0.15/word

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Domiciliation and registered agent services (first year)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for VAT and registration duties; unified electronic business portal: MyGuichet.lu (professional space, eCDF e-filing) and the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS/LBR) database.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Notarize the SCSp partnership deed and file it with the RCS Luxembourg to obtain the RCS registration number and the matricule national. Step 2: Submit the single business and VAT registration application (Form 510) through MyGuichet.lu to the AED to obtain the Luxembourg VAT identification number (format LU + 8 digits); a non-established foreign entity must appoint a Luxembourg fiscal representative for VAT and enclose its foreign VAT registration certificate and commercial-register excerpt. Step 3: Register the direct-tax profile with the ACD: the SCSp remains fiscally transparent by default, so the partners are assessed on their allocable shares via Form 500 (individuals) or Form 520 (corporate partners); the SCSp itself obtains a separate corporate-tax file only if the Article 175(1) LIR commercial-activity exception to transparency applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default for CIT, municipal business tax (MBT) and net wealth tax; there is no US-style check-the-box. Article 175bis LIR permits a partnership not exploiting a commercial enterprise to elect irrevocably to be taxed as a corporation (binding for at least 5 tax years). A fulfillment/kitting operation constitutes a commercial activity and may therefore trigger entity-level CIT/MBT under Article 175(1) LIR, which can be mitigated through a Luxembourg advance tax ruling (tax confirmation) on the intended partner-level allocation. ATAD II hybrid-mismatch rules override any elective treatment and require payment and invoice flows to be aligned with the transparent status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée - TVA) under the amended Law of 12 February 1979, conforming to EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 annual turnover for the established small-enterprise franchise (Article 94 of the VAT Law); non-established foreign suppliers are registrable from the first taxable supply in Luxembourg, subject to reverse charge where the customer is a taxable person (B2B place-of-supply rules).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2G e-invoicing since 1 January 2024 via the Peppol eDelivery network (eSpace) for invoices addressed to the Luxembourg State and public-sector bodies; no general mandatory B2B real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous-transaction-control API applies to the kitting/fulfillment sector; B2B e-invoicing remains optional, and VAT is settled periodically on the periodic VAT return (Form 1001).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to (i) goods physically exported outside the EU, evidenced by transport and dispatch documentation proving departure from EU territory; (ii) ancillary services directly related to those goods, including freight handling, palletization, kitting, assembly and storage, supplied by the operator; and (iii) services supplied to non-EU B2B customers where the place of supply is outside Luxembourg. Intra-EU B2B dispatches from Luxembourg fulfillment centers are exempt with credit for input VAT, requiring the customer's valid EU VAT number and EC Sales List declaration. Luxembourg law does not impose a calendrical FX-repatriation deadline for VAT zero-rating; the 180-day benchmark is retained as the internal documentary-compliance standard for proving genuine export consideration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/DAU lodged electronically with the Luxembourg customs authorities, or the export manifest for postal and express consignments)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport document evidencing physical departure of the goods from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate (SWIFT/MT103 or bank credit advice evidencing receipt of the foreign-currency payment from the non-EU buyer)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AED may reassess VAT within the standard 5-year limitation period, extended to 10 years in cases of fraud or evasion. Unjustified zero-rating triggers retrospective clawback of the VAT due plus statutory late-payment interest, administrative fines under Article 50 of the VAT Law (EUR 50 to EUR 1,000 per infringement) and, in cases of deliberate fraud, criminal fines and imprisonment. The exporter bears the burden of proof and is jointly and severally liable for any input VAT recovered on zero-rated transactions that fail audit verification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); regulatory coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for AML/CFT, banking supervision, and payment service provider licensing under Luxembourg law of 5 April 1993 and CSSF prudential rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg, as a euro-area Member State, applies full liberalisation of capital movements and current payments in accordance with Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Directive 88/361/EEC. There are no foreign exchange controls, no BCL licensing gates, and no prior approval requirements for conversion between EUR, USD, GBP, CHF, or other freely convertible currencies. Both current account transactions (trade payments, services, wages) and capital account transactions (capital contributions, loan repayments, distributions, return of capital) are freely convertible and freely remittable. Profit remittance constraints are de minimis: remittances by an SCSp are blocked only by ordinary AML/KYC screening, transfer-of-funds information requirements under EU Regulation 2015/847, and sanctions compliance. The SCSp has no Luxembourg tax on profits at entity level because it is tax-transparent, but profit withdrawals paid to partners must satisfy source-of-funds and beneficial ownership documentation to prevent bank refusal on money-laundering risk grounds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement in Luxembourg. No period is prescribed for repatriation, and no percentage of trade receivables must be converted into EUR. Export proceeds from fulfilment, kitting, and assembly services may be retained in the original invoice currency or freely swapped into EUR, USD, or any other permitted currency. Banks may, however, require a commercial contract or customs/transport document for the receipt to remain within the permitted 'low-risk standard' tier under the CSSF AML framework, and all inbound export collections must be traceable to named counterparties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital escrow account, operational EUR/USD settlement account, FX hedging custody account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Luxembourg IBAN operational treasury account; partner capital deposit sub-ledger
Multi-currency operational account, trade finance and commercial letter of credit settlement account
Operational treasury account, escrow overlay account for third-party logistics collections
Private-banking and partnership treasury account for SCSp holding structures

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for operating cash flows, Low for regulated capital or escrow arrangements. Luxembourg permits CSSF-licensed or EU/EEA-passported e-money institutions and payment institutions to issue payment accounts to commercial clients under PSD2. An SCSp engaged in kitting and 3PL fulfilment can open multi-currency payment accounts with Airwallex, Currencycloud, or similar EMIs to collect low-value retailer/brand payouts and disburse supplier invoices in USD, GBP, and EUR with API automation. Legal constraints: no non-EU EMI may provide Luxembourg IBANs without a proper EU/EAA e-money licence or agent arrangement; EMI accounts are not bank deposits and fall outside the Luxembourg Deposit Guarantee Scheme of the FGDL; such accounts cannot be used for issuance/acceptance of documentary credits, do not provide counterparty credit facilities, and are not suitable as custodial capital escrow accounts. For the low-risk logistical receivables flows they are, however, a viable treasury rail because of lower onboarding friction, competitive FX spreads, and SWIFT/local-network settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The SCSp is an unregulated special limited partnership without legal personality, represented by its general partner. There is no blanket statutory requirement under Luxembourg law for all directors of every SCSp to appear physically before a bank; onboarding is risk-based under the Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02. Remote opening by secure video interview is generally acceptable for a low-risk SCSp when the general partner is an EU or Luxembourg entity, beneficial owners are identified with recognised ID, and a notarised copy of the partnership agreement is supplied. Nevertheless, in practice, most tier-one Luxembourg banks mandate at least one in-person meeting of the authorised representative or director, or, alternatively, a Luxembourg-based professional intermediary (lawyer, notary, or fund administrator) to certify identity. Physical appearance is effectively unavoidable if the general partner is non-EU resident, if a limited partner owns more than 25% and resides in a high-risk jurisdiction, or if the bank categorises the incoming 3PL flow as high-volume and potentially commingled.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp has no separate legal personality, creating ambiguity on account ownership and signatory binding authority.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified notarised partnership agreement; written designation of the general partner; Commercial register extract from the Luxembourg Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés or RBEL; management resolution of the general partner appointing authorised signatories; passport copies of signatories; account mandate form signed by the GP.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered partnership chain containing non-resident limited partners triggers complex beneficial ownership identification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full beneficial ownership organisational chart with percentages of ownership and voting rights; CSSF-compliant UBO declaration listing every natural person ultimately holding or controlling more than 25%; certified IDs and proof of residential address for each UBO; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds narratives; confirmation that the SCSp has not issued bearer shares.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume fulfilment and kitting receivables resemble commingled merchant settlements and trigger transaction monitoring flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master 3PL and kitting agreements with ecommerce retailers; sample pick/pack/kitting invoices and delivery proof; supply-chain contracts with component vendors; comprehensive AML risk assessment classifying the activity as low-risk standard; documented client vetting procedure; transaction monitoring policies and quarterly reconciliation reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments originating from or destined to counterparties in AML/CFT high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-onboarding sanctions and adverse media screening results; jurisdiction risk assessment explanation; detailed commercial purpose statement; copies of export/import declarations and transport documents; enhanced due diligence file including beneficial ownership of each sensitive counterparty; contractual clauses mandating anti-money-laundering and sanctions compliance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Supply-chain vendor payments mixed with capital contributions in the same account, clouding audit trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Segregation by establishing a dedicated capital escrow sub-account for partner contributions and a separate operational settlement account; accounting policy statement distinguishing equity, trade payables and expense refunds; monthly bank account reconciliation; partner capital call letters with unique contribution references; independent accountant attestation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Partner capital injections into the SCSp must be routed through SEPA Credit Transfer (for EUR from EU/EEA accounts) or SWIFT MT103 / MT202 COV (for non-EU contributions or USD/GBP conversions), using the SCSp's dedicated capital sub-account to ensure traceability. The remittance instructions must include the full name and address of the transferring partner, the SCSp legal name, and a structured reference such as 'SCSP-CAP-INV-YYYYMMDD-001' equal to the capital call document. For non-EU remittances, the bank requires an indication of the economic purpose code corresponding to foreign direct investment or partnership equity acquisition, supported by the notarised or written partnership agreement; no BCL foreign-exchange approval is needed. The receiving Luxembourg bank will verify that the remitting partner is the actual holder of the sending account and that the source of funds is compatible with the declared wealth; where funds pass through an intermediary, the full payment chain must be visible under Article 4 of EU Regulation 2015/847.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The blueprint uses SEPA Credit Transfer for all EUR-denominated vendor payments within the EEA, leveraging the Luxembourg Target2 membership and instant SEPA settlement rails. For non-EUR supplier invoices, trade settlements are executed via SWIFT MT103 with corresponding bank cover, or MT202 COV for high-value intercompany reimbursements. Commercial letters of credit (documentary credits governed by UCP600 and ISP98 where required) are available through tier-one Luxembourg banks for international purchase of kitting components; issuance is by MT700 with MT707 amendments, with presentation documents routed through the nominated or confirming bank. For smaller, repetitive supplier payments and marketplace fee disbursements, the treasury overlay uses Airwallex local clearing routes in supported currencies, with automatic conversion into EUR at day-end and sweep to the primary BIL or Spuerkeess account. The outbound treasury team must maintain audit evidence of each disbursement: supplier invoice, purchase order, packing list, and sanctions/screen result per beneficiary.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward FX contracts (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, USD/EUR) with a licensed Luxembourg bank or EU investment firm under the ISDA Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex, provided the underlying exposure is a signed supplier invoice or forecast purchase order.
Window or rolling forwards allowing periodic USD procurement hedges for kitting component imports without fixing every individual invoice.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with settlement restrictions, e.g., offshore CNY, receivable from emerging-market e-commerce counterparties, cleared in USD/EUR offshore and documented with a trade rationale.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCS / CCIRS) solely for minimising basis risk on a committed multi-year USD supply agreement and matching EUR funding; no speculative option positions are permitted under the SCSp treasury policy.

At-the-money FX spot-limit orders executed through the bank's electronic dealing platform without leverage, and FX swaps for temporary liquidity in EUR/USD, subject to daily counterparty credit limits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (RBE annual declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of the initial RBE filing; updated filings within 30 days of any ownership or control change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Continued non-compliance restricts distributions, voting rights, and exercise of financial rights; criminal fines apply under the Law of 13 January 2019; prolonged default is recorded at the RBE and may lead to court-ordered strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and balance sheet filing (required only where Luxembourg accounting law, the partnership agreement, or an audit regime makes filing mandatory; a default transparent SCSp is generally exempt from RCS publication)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Where applicable, within 1 month of partner approval and no later than 7 months after the balance sheet date; partner approval must occur within 6 months of the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a public prosecutor summons, court-ordered coercive fines (astreinte), general partner civil liability, and, after formal notice, administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax and net wealth tax declaration (only if the SCSp has elected opaque corporate taxation; default pass-through treatment requires no entity-level corporate income tax return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (Luxembourg tax authorities, ACD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For an opaque-electing SCSp, the annual return follows the ACD assessment calendar; for calendar-year taxpayers the filing form is generally due by 31 December of the following year, subject to extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the general partner to default interest, late-payment interest, tax penalties of up to 10% of the taxes due, enforced collection, and criminal sanctions for willful non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual internal audit of statutory registers, partnership interest transfers, and corporate minutes (non-governmental corporate secretarial measure supporting RBE confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed; maintained at the registered office or by the corporate service provider
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing; formal review recommended before each annual RBE confirmation and before the annual partner meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete registers impair the accuracy of UBO declarations and may trigger RBE penalties; defective transfer documentation can undermine partners' limited liability protection and delay distributions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Luxembourg mandatory independent audit by a réviseur d'entreprises agréé applies when an entity exceeds two of the three thresholds on the balance sheet date: balance sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, or average headcount above 50. A SCSp may also be required to appoint an auditor under its partnership agreement, as an alternative investment fund or regulated vehicle, or upon partner request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial accounts (transposing Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS is mandatory for consolidated accounts and listed entities and may be used for statutory accounts where permitted or required by investors.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each SCSp registered in the Luxembourg RBE must submit an annual confirmation within 30 days after the anniversary of its initial beneficial-owner declaration; any change in ownership or control must be reported within one month. The confirmation must state all natural persons who ultimately own or control the SCSp, including indirect control through the general partner, and must be supported by accurate internal registers of partners and transfers.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of partnership interests / quota transfers
Register of pledges and usufructs over partnership interests

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 15,000 per year for a small operational SCSp; higher where consolidated or fund-regulated

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City aggregate: 17% corporate income tax + 7% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax); SCSp is fiscally transparent and is not subject to entity-level corporate income tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is tax transparent: no CIT, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax at the SCSp level. Each partner is taxed on their allocated share. Qualifying corporate partners may benefit from the Luxembourg participation exemption, including a 100% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains, subject to a 10% holding threshold and 12-month holding period (or acquisition commitment). No statutory licence is required for low-risk kitting/fulfilment activities under ISIC 5210.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 / MyGuichet.lu with LuxTrust electronic signature; used for corporate income tax and municipal business tax reporting where required. A fiscally transparent SCSp generally files an annual informational return/annex rather than a standalone CIT return unless a Luxembourg permanent establishment is treated as reportable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Luxembourg tax administration normally requires filing by 30 June of the year following the fiscal year-end for calendar-year taxpayers; extensions may be granted upon formal request before the deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCS number, Luxembourg tax matricule, registered office, legal form (SCSp), fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Luxembourg registered office and local representative details. Non-resident partners need not be entered as taxpayers unless they have a Luxembourg permanent establishment through the SCSp's commercial operations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the financial year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must match the audited financial statements and the partnership deed; non-resident investors should align reporting with their home-country tax year only if the Luxembourg permanent establishment result is integrated under a treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss before tax adjustments, including revenue from fulfilment, kitting, assembly, storage, and ancillary logistics services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Because the SCSp is transparent, the aggregate result is allocated according to the partnership agreement; each non-resident partner reports only the Luxembourg-source allocable share unless protected and recharacterized by a tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 — Tax adjustments and non-deductible expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses, fines, excessive remuneration, intra-group charges not at arm's length, and any tax-exempt income adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Applies at the SCSp computation level to determine allocable net income; non-resident partners must retain the allocation schedule to support their home-country foreign tax credit or exemption claim.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying dividends and capital gains from a qualifying subsidiary, provided the 10% threshold and 12-month holding condition are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to the SCSp itself unless it is treated as opaque for tax purposes; a corporate partner claiming the Luxembourg participation exemption must hold through a qualifying Luxembourg structure and maintain full economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, residence, tax identification number, profit/loss sharing percentage, and distributive share of each partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must provide valid tax residence certificates and, if treaty relief is sought, a completed beneficial ownership declaration. Distributions from a transparent SCSp are not subject to Luxembourg dividend withholding tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing can trigger an administrative fine up to EUR 3,000, a surcharge of up to 10% of assessed tax, and monthly late-payment interest. Material misstatements or deliberate omissions are treated as tax fraud, exposing the taxpayer to criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years, in addition to re-assessment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on distributions made by a transparent SCSp because such distributions are partnership profit distributions, not dividends. The Luxembourg statutory dividend withholding tax rate for ordinary opaque companies is 15%, and may be reduced or exempted under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or a double taxation treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident partner seeking treaty relief must submit a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the partner's jurisdiction of residence to the Luxembourg withholding agent before the distribution date, together with a beneficial ownership declaration and the partnership agreement. If withholding was applied ex post, a refund claim must be filed with the Luxembourg direct tax administration before the end of the relevant statutory limitation period (generally 5 years), attaching the TRC, audited accounts, allocation schedule, and confirmation of beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Outbound royalty payments: 0% Luxembourg withholding tax under domestic law. Outbound interest payments: 0% general withholding tax; special 20% Luxembourg final withholding tax may apply to certain retail savings interest paid to Luxembourg resident individuals. Treaty and EU Interest-Royalty Directive rates are commonly 0% for qualifying corporate beneficial owners.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The Luxembourg Country-by-Country Reporting threshold is EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue. The Luxembourg tax administration may require transfer pricing documentation for any material related-party transaction, and in practice expects robust contemporaneous documentation for SCSp transactions with related parties above EUR 100,000, even absent a formal statutory Local File threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive and Luxembourg general anti-abuse rules require genuine economic substance. An SCSp engaged in fulfilment kitting and assembly must maintain a Luxembourg registered office, a resident corporate general partner, decision-making records, bank account, payroll or subcontracting capacity for actual operations, and books showing that the partners assume real risk and control. Artificial arrangements without substance will be challenged, and treaty benefits may be denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and undeclared Luxembourg-source income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-resident partner omits its allocable share of SCSp profits derived from Luxembourg fulfilment/kitting service activities; false partner allocations; use of nominee partners to conceal the ultimate beneficiary.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative surcharge up to 50% of the evaded tax plus late-payment interest; criminal prosecution for tax fraud with imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 250,000; treaty relief is denied and the SCSp may be recharacterized as opaque and taxed at 24.94%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner who knowingly cause or participate in tax evasion can be held personally liable for unpaid taxes and penalties under abuse-of-rights and fraud doctrines; travel bans, asset seizures, and extradition requests may arise in cross-border criminal tax proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / artificial arrangement / sham SCSp
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SCSp has no real employees, no premises, no operational decision-making, and no commercial substance in Luxembourg; it is used merely as an invoicing or flow-through vehicle for foreign related parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the SCSp as a taxable Luxembourg entity; comprehensive reassessment at the combined 24.94% rate; denial of double taxation treaty benefits; imputation of hidden profits; 10% late-payment interest and significant fines; EU ATAD GAAR countermeasures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner may be personally liable for the resulting tax deficiency if they orchestrated the sham; disqualification from managing Luxembourg companies and travel bans are available measures in serious cross-border abuse cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence or file the Luxembourg beneficial ownership register; concealing the real beneficiary behind layered partner structures; executing payments through ACH/Airwallex without documenting the commercial purpose or underlying principal.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Luxembourg AML/CFT law, imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 500,000 for individuals; legal persons may face administrative fines up to EUR 5,000,000; suspension of management and publication of the sanction are possible.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers of the SCSp's general partner are personally exposed to criminal sanctions and disqualification if they knowingly facilitated money laundering or breached beneficial ownership disclosure duties; assets may be frozen and travel restricted during investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing manipulation and false documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp charges non-arm's-length amounts to foreign group affiliates for kitting, assembly, and fulfilment services; no contemporaneous transfer pricing study; no proof of actual service performance or capacity; fabricated invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary transfer pricing adjustment to taxable income, secondary adjustments, denial of cost deductions, interest accrual, and fines for gross negligence up to 50% of the deficiency; criminal fraud exposure if false documentation is used.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Chief officers and directors who sign or approve false transfer pricing documentation may be jointly and severally liable for the additional tax; personal fines and imprisonment apply under fraud provisions; professional disqualification may be ordered.
